imem_words.doc: Program memory depth in 32-bit words. Capped at 256 by the ISA: BR and CALL targets are eight bits, so a larger store holds unreachable words. The pinned CMOS5L PDK contains no compatible SRAM macro views; the early-flow profile therefore uses 64 words of inferred storage, the smallest power-of-two depth that holds every mandatory demo, while the default remains 256 until measured flow evidence settles the architecture. The assembler refuses a program longer than this value. The store is single-port and synchronous-read; the host has the same eight-bit ceiling.

reg_count.doc: General registers R0..R(n-1). Costs reg_count * reg_width flip-flops against a whole-die ceiling near 7,680, so this is one of the few knobs that trades directly against the instruction store.

reg_width.doc: Register width in bits. Also the widest value SHOUT/SHIN can move in one instruction and the widest measurement WAITE can return, so narrowing it shortens the longest interval the chip can time.

delay_bits.doc: Width of the delay field every instruction carries, and therefore the longest single hold or WAITE timeout in cycles. Also the width of the period register SHPER writes, since that holds the same kind of value the cell timer counts: narrowing one without the other would let the register hold a period the timer cannot reach. At 50 MHz, 16 bits reaches 1.31 ms, which covers one bit time down to about 763 baud.

uio_pins.doc: Bidirectional protocol pins, each with its own direction and open-drain control. The Tiny Tapeout harness supplies 8; a profile targeting another carrier may have fewer.

call_depth.doc: Hardware call stack entries. Each costs clog2(imem_words) flip-flops. Firmware that exceeds it is a build-time error in the assembler rather than a silent overwrite.
